source: Heat moves from warmer things to cooler things. It moves by touching (conduction), by moving air or water (convection) and by rays like sunshine (radiation). Insulators slow it down.
Thinking a sweater or blanket makes heat. It keeps your own body heat from escaping; wrap a sweater around an ice cube and the ice stays cold longer.
Hold a mug of hot cocoa and your hands warm up. Put an ice cube in your hand and your hand gets cold. Heat is on the move.

Heat moves from warmer things to cooler things, never the other way by itself. It moves three ways: by touching (conduction), by moving air or water carrying it (convection), and by rays through space, like sunshine (radiation).
A metal spoon in hot soup gets hot all the way up because metal passes heat along quickly. A wooden spoon stays cool at the top because wood is an insulator.
Does a sweater make you warm by making heat?
No: it keeps your body heat in.
A sweater has no energy source.
It traps air, an insulator, so your own body heat escapes slowly.
Thinking cold "moves in". Your hand feels cold on ice because heat leaves your hand and goes into the ice.
